content.title: Service Line Replacement Program Details
content.summary: As of March 5, 2024, all lead drinking water service lines are banned in Arvada, including galvanized lines installed before 1960, with property owners required to replace them by December 31, 2026. The City of Arvada will fund the replacement of identified lead service lines, and property owners must coordinate with the City’s contractor for scheduling and sign a consent form to participate in the program. Residents can contact the City's Water Quality team for assistance and further details.
content.body:
For the protection of public health and the betterment of the community, as of March 5, 2024, **all lead drinking water service lines are prohibited** from use within Arvada’s water service boundaries. The definition of a Lead Service Line (LSL) for the purpose of this program also includes all galvanized water service lines installed before 1960.

The property owner is responsible for ensuring any lead water service line is replaced on or before **December 31, 2026**.

The following information outlines the program details and applicability for the City of Arvada Lead Service Line Replacement Program (LSLRP or Program). The requirements are based on the [March 4, 2024 City Council Ordinance and updates to the Arvada City Code](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/ordinances/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=1277009). This fulfills the requirements of the USEPA Lead and Copper Rule, Colorado Regulation 11, and accompanying Policies.

![service line connection to water main showing customer and system owned portions of a water line](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4697)

## Applicability

1. This Program applies to any existing or future drinking water service line connections to buildings or structures identified as having service line materials made of lead or unknown material, that receive water service directly from the City’s drinking water utility. This Program does not apply to structures within consecutive water systems receiving City finished water or residents not on City water.
2. This Program applies specifically to **customer-owned service lines**. All system-owned service lines and connectors are presumed to be non-lead, but will be immediately (within 5 business days) replaced upon any discovery of lead or galvanized materials.
3. Please contact the City's Water Quality team to coordinate applicable service line replacement.
   - [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#cb8788998baab9bdaaafaae5a4b9ac)
   - 720-898-7800

## May 1, 2024 through December 31, 2026

1. [City funded replacement](#tab54a8dc89-3c9c-4fd6-9990-ef65d98b155f_0)

## City funded replacement

With owner consent, the City will pay for and provide full service line replacement, from meter to point of entry (“foundation”), for all identified Lead Service Lines (LSL) as defined in the Arvada City Code.

1. The property owner will coordinate with the City’s contractor for scheduling of replacement. The contractor will schedule replacements based on efficiency, but may try to accommodate individual schedules if possible or necessary.
   - It is the owner's responsibility to notify any occupants of the home of the work being performed if owner does not reside in the building.
2. All work will be performed according to the [City’s Engineering Standards](/167). The City’s contractor will acquire the proper locates, permits, and inspections.
   - Note: customers in Arvada’s water district but outside of city limits may also require a county permit.
3. Any owner participating in the City’s free replacement program must sign and submit a Service Line Replacement consent form. This will be provided by either the City’s Water Quality Division or the contractor. The consent form explains the responsibilities of the City/contractor and owner/occupant.
4. The City or its contractor will provide instructions to the occupant for internal water pipe flushing to remove any particulates from the service line and premise plumbing after replacement. A lead-reducing pitcher filter with 6 months’ worth of filters will be available upon request (please allow up to 3 business days for delivery).
5. Any complaints related to the work performed for this project should first be communicated directly to the contractor to resolve. Any unresolved disputes should then be communicated to the Water Quality Division.
6. Any property damage claims related to the work performed for this project may be submitted to City's Risk Department.

1. [Owner funded replacement](#tab54a8dc89-3c9c-4fd6-9990-ef65d98b155f_1)

If the property owner prefers to replace their own service line at their own expense, they may do so as long as the work is performed in accordance with the [City’s Engineering Standards](/167) (including any required locates, permits, and inspections).

1. A [Right-of-Way Water/Sewer Service permit](/660) will need to be issued with the description to read “LSL Water Service Line Replacement” and inspection scheduled.
2. All work must be reported to the City's Water Quality Division, so records can be updated and the property can be removed from the service line notification list.
3. Flushing instructions and a lead-reducing pitcher filter with 6 months’ worth of filters will be available upon request (please allow up to 3 business days for delivery).
4. The city will **not** provide reimbursement for any self-work performed between May 1, 2024 and December 31, 2026.

1. [Reimbursement for previous replacement](#tab54a8dc89-3c9c-4fd6-9990-ef65d98b155f_2)

For a Lead Service Line (LSL) that was previously replaced between December 1, 2021 and April 30, 2024, the City will reimburse the invoice up to $8,000 provided that:

1. Owner provides evidence of previous material replaced and invoices for work.
   - If evidence of previous material does not exist, please call the City's Water Quality Division to discuss.
2. Owner complied with the [City’s Engineering Standards](/167) for all work performed, including obtaining appropriate permits and inspections.
3. Owner has not previously been reimbursed by another party or insurance provider.
4. Submit the [**Reimbursement Request Form**](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/40839) with the required documentation attached.

No reimbursement requests will be accepted after December 31, 2026.

1. [Before & After photos](#tab54a8dc89-3c9c-4fd6-9990-ef65d98b155f_3)

## January 1, 2027 or later

1. [Known or discovered lead service line](#tab0506152b-ff62-4240-90b8-49e8d17134f5_0)

For any known remaining or newly discovered LSL in the system.

1. Property owners with a known Lead Service Line (LSL) will receive a Service Line Notification letter annually until replaced.
2. Owners must replace their service line **at their own expense**.
3. Owners must perform replacement in accordance with the [City’s Engineering Specifications](/167). A [Right-of-Way Water/Sewer Service permit](/660) will need to be issued with the description to read “LSL Water Service Line Replacement” and an inspection scheduled.
4. Owner must provide proof of replacement to the City's Water Quality Division within 182 days of notice from the City.
   - A one time extension of this timeframe may be granted if requested within 28 days.
5. If a property owner has a known or discovered LSL, and does not replace it within 182 days after notice from the city, they will be **subject to fines of $1,000 per year until replaced.**
6. Prior to the LSL replacement (and no later than 6 months after replacement), **if requested,** the City will provide occupant with internal pipe flushing instructions and a lead-reducing pitcher filter with 6 months’ worth of filters (please allow up to 3 business days for delivery).
7. Within 3-6 months after replacement, **if requested,** the City will provide a bottle for customer to collect a tap sample for lead analysis.

1. [Unknown service line material](#tab0506152b-ff62-4240-90b8-49e8d17134f5_1)

For remaining “Unknown” service line materials in the system.

1. Property owners with an “Unknown” service line material will receive a Service Line Notification letter annually until categorized. Owners must notify the City’s Water Quality Division of the service line material within 63 days, otherwise they will be treated as Lead Service Lines (LSL) and **subject to fines of $1,000 per year until replaced or confirmed non-lead.**
   - Please call the Water Quality Division if you need assistance determining your service line material.
2. Properties confirmed non-lead will be removed from the Program.
3. Properties with confirmed LSL must follow the requirements listed in the known or discovered lead service line section above.

1. [Additional Information](#tab0506152b-ff62-4240-90b8-49e8d17134f5_2)

1. All property owners that have a Lead Service Line (LSL) replaced must notify the City’s Water Quality Division to have records updated and be removed from the Program.
2. No new connection to Arvada’s water system that has an existing LSL or “Unknown” will be permitted until the service line is replaced or confirmed non-lead.
3. **Fines for non-compliance**.
   - A fine assessment of $1,000 will be assessed annually for all non-compliant properties.
   - Any appeals to a fine must be made within 14 days of issuance.
   - Fines left unpaid for 63 days from issue date may be subject to a property lien with the county, which can impede the selling of the home.
4. For owners who are unable to afford to replace their LSL, financial assistance will be available.

1. [Financial Assistance Program](#tab0506152b-ff62-4240-90b8-49e8d17134f5_3)

### Applicability

1. ### 

   Property owners who did not participate in the City’s free replacement program and replace a known Lead Service Line (LSL) prior to January 1, 2027, and who provide evidence of financial need.
   - Income eligibility criteria will be based on household size using the most current Affordable Gross Income Limits for Jefferson County.
   - Any unpaid fines owed to the city for the Program will be deducted from the eligible amount of reimbursement.
2. A new property owner that acquires a home that has an LSL, previously known or unknown.
3. The property’s service line was previously misidentified as non-lead, and it is later determined to be LSL.

## Process

Owner must submit a Financial Assistance Request Form and attach all necessary documentation.

1. The City will reimburse up to $6000 of the cost of the invoice for the replacement. Other payment option/plan requests may be considered, but must be approved by the City prior to beginning work.
2. The City will waive all permit and inspection fees if “LSL Water Service Line Replacement” is noted when requesting permits.
3. Property owners must adhere to the [City’s Engineering Specifications](/167) for replacement, provide proof of active service line material prior to replacement, and retain all receipts of work for submittal.
4. LSL must be replaced within 182 days of discovery or possession, and notification sent to the City's Water Quality Division.

## General program information

1. [Internal Plumbing Flushing Instructions](#tabb77d5cc0-c9af-413f-986d-638a46a4605e_0)

The potholing investigation or service line replacement can cause disturbance in your service line from the meter to your foundation.

After the City's contractor performs potholing or replacement work on your drinking water service line, it is advised that you flush your internal (premise) plumbing before using the water, especially if you notice any discoloration or particulate matter. Flushing will minimize any exposure to lead or other metal release that may have occurred. You may need to repeat the flushing occasionally as needed for up to three months.

### Flush all your faucets using these steps:

1. Remove faucet aerators and screens (if possible) from all cold water taps in the home.
2. Beginning in the lowest level of the home and working your way to the highest level, fully open all the **cold** water taps throughout the home. Be sure to run water in bathtubs and showers as well. Do not use hot water.
3. Let the cold water run for 10-30 minutes.
4. Turn off each tap starting with the taps in the highest level of the home, working your way back down.
5. Clean the aerators/screens before reattaching on faucets, and replace if old or worn.
6. Do not consume tap water, open hot water faucets, or use icemakers or filtered water dispensers until after flushing is complete.

You may also wish to temporarily use a point-of-use filter for water to be used for drinking and cooking, particularly if you are pregnant or have children under age six. If your service line was replaced under the City's program, you may request a lead-reducing pitcher filter which is good for 6 months of use. Please contact the Water Quality Department to request.

If discoloration occurs for more than 24 hours, or if you have any other questions or concerns, please contact the Water Quality Department.

1. [Recordkeeping and tracking](#tabb77d5cc0-c9af-413f-986d-638a46a4605e_1)

1. All communication records and owner-submitted forms will be kept on file at the City for at least 12 years.
2. [Arvada's Service Line Inventory map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=960927ac3a7a4dccb104c3440fea172a) will be updated periodically with any new information. Please notify the City’s Water Quality Division of any discrepancies.

1. [Communications](#tabb77d5cc0-c9af-413f-986d-638a46a4605e_2)

1. No later than November 2024, the City’s Water Quality Division will mail an initial Service Line Notification letter to all properties with an LSL or “Unknown” water service line with information on how to determine the material and/or notify the City’s Water Quality Division, along with information about the LSLRP.
   - The Service Line Notification letter will be sent annually in April each subsequent year.
2. Other Program communication formats may include direct mail postcards, fliers, door hangers, emails, phone calls, or in person interactions.
3. Designated email for all Lead/Program-related inquiries: [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#602c2332200112160104014e0f1207).
4. Webpage for all Lead-related information: [ArvadaCO.gov/Water-Quality-Lead](/841).
